statement.p: Find the second-degree Taylor polynomial for f(x)=5 x^2 - 6 x + 7 about x=0.
What do you notice about your polynomial?

static.solution:
f(0) = 7; f'(x) = 10 x - 6, so that f'(0) = -6; and f''(x) = 10, so that f''(0) = 10.
Thus T_2(x) = 7 - 6 x + {10\over 2!} x^2 = 7 - 6 x + 5 x^2.
We notice that f(x) = T_2(x) in this case, which makes sense because f(x) is a polynomial.
